newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Gold may test $340 after OTC expiry.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold may test $340 after OTC expiry.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Gold will hover around $341-$342 an ounce for most of Monday, but may then retreat to test support at $340 after the expiry of OTC options, analysts and traders said.
Silver's fortunes would depend on gold with key support at $4.65.
Platinum might ease but with a tight forward market capping losses.
GOLD - The market is likely to stay glued to a narrow range between $341 and $342 early with options-related buying coming into play at around $340.
But Monday's OTC expiry at 1330 GMT might spell the end of gold's upside prospects for now with an imminent test of $340 seen possible.
"I think the $342-$342.50 was well tested on Friday but it refuses to break on the upside," said one dealer, adding that $340 would be put to the test severely this week, possibly late on Monday.
"$339 will probably hold for the moment. But it will try lower levels later in the week," said the dealer. "It would be adventurous to buy the market. The best thing is to go short."
Support came in at the recent low of $337.50 first, followed by the February 12 low of $336.15, although at that level good physical demand was expected to emerge.

At the weekend Group of Seven meeting the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said it hoped to use existing resources and biletaral contributions to fund its debt relief plan to poor countries, but an official said gold sales could be an option later.

"The longer we wait to sell gold, the less interest income," said Jack Boorman, director of the IMF's policy development and review department. "(But) we have not yet reached the point where that decision has to be taken," he added.
The dollar was edging off its highs after a benign statement on currencies from the G7.
At 0800 GMT, gold was quoted at $341.45 from Friday's New York close of $341.90/2.40.
